about: The setup a product needs before a job starts (setup audit, 2 Nov 2026). One entry per condition. `p3 setup check` reads each one it can: GitHub through gh api, the tranche's files through git, the session's own checkout and environment, and, for the deploy token only, harmless reads of Cloudflare's API; and reports it as set or missing. The proxy refuses GitHub's Actions-settings, secrets, collaborators and environments endpoints, so those conditions are confirmed once on the onboarding page and never read. `job start` runs the same check first. A condition whose `who` starts with "the developer" is the repository owner's to set; setup/DEVELOPER.md holds the steps.

conditions.what: The account sessions act as can push to the product and is not an admin of it.
conditions.why: Sessions push their own branches and open pull requests. An admin could bypass every ruleset and change settings.
conditions.who: the developer (the repository's owner): adds the session account as a collaborator and points Claude's GitHub connection at it
conditions.read: GET /user for the account, then GET /repos/{repo}: permissions.push and permissions.admin

conditions.what: An active ruleset on every branch, with nothing excluded, refuses deletion and force-push, and the session account cannot bypass it.
conditions.why: No session may delete a branch or rewrite history, on any branch (the standing safety rules).
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Rules)
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets, then GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets/{id}: conditions.ref_name, rules, current_user_can_bypass

conditions.what: main and the tranche take changes only through a pull request, merged with a merge commit only, with the required check green and no approving review required; the session account cannot bypass these rules.
conditions.why: The gate is what makes a merge trustworthy; merge commits keep each pull request's history whole.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Rules)
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/rules/branches/{branch} for main and the tranche: pull_request.allowed_merge_methods, required_approving_review_count, require_code_owner_review and required_reviewers and required_status_checks; GET /repos/{repo}/rulesets/{id}: current_user_can_bypass

conditions.what: No classic branch protection rule is on main or the tranche; the rulesets alone hold them.
conditions.why: An older classic rule was missed on 2 Nov; a classic rule adds requirements (reviews, admins exempt or not) that the rulesets and the tool do not expect, and its bypasses cannot be read by a session.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Branches, Branch protection rules: Delete)
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/branches/{branch} for main and the tranche: protected and protection.enabled; GET /repos/{repo}/branches/{branch}/protection where readable. A rule found is reported missing, to remove; a branch not pushed yet is unmeasured

conditions.what: The repository allows merge commits, does not allow auto-merge, and does not delete a branch when its pull request merges.
conditions.why: Merges are made by the tool alone, with a merge commit; no branch is ever deleted.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, General)
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}: allow_merge_commit, allow_auto_merge, delete_branch_on_merge

conditions.what: The tranche's .claude/settings.json denies force-push, branch deletion, writing files through GitHub, and every merge route but the tool; and no rule in it refuses a command the process tells a session to run (its push is `p3 github push`).
conditions.why: The deny list holds the standing safety rules in every session; the tool's merge is the one route (Bob's CLAUDE.md approvals, 2 Nov). A rule that refuses a told command (its push among them) leaves a session at a refusal no one sees; each Bash rule is matched against every command the process tells, as Claude Code matches it, by the one check admit.mjs holds (C3, C17). Changes to the settings file itself are held by the record check, which finds any change that is not the owner's own website commit.
conditions.who: the developer, committing it on the tranche through GitHub's website; a session cannot edit its own settings file
conditions.read: the file on origin/<tranche>, through git: permissions.deny, each Bash rule matched against the commands the pinned tool and its rulebooks tell a session to run (admit.mjs)

conditions.what: CLAUDE.md on the tranche holds one approvals block, under the heading process/config.json names, the one the owner's own commit through GitHub's website last set on the tranche or main.
conditions.why: A session acts on the owner's standing approvals only when CLAUDE.md holding them is on the branch it starts from (10 of 10 with it, 2 of 10 without; Bob, 2 Nov, before the log; unverified). Only the owner's own website commit may set them, so a session cannot widen its own approvals.

value.heading: process/config.json approvals.heading, default ## Standing approvals from Bob
value.owner: process/config.json approvals.owner (neobobkrause when it names none), which the owner confirms once at onboarding
value.last_set_by: the owner's commit through GitHub's website, on the tranche or main, the newer of the two

conditions.who: the developer, committing it on the tranche through GitHub's website, signed in as the owner
conditions.read: the file on origin/<tranche>, through git: the approvals headings; then, for origin/<tranche> and origin/main, one git log of the file (in a shallow clone, never deepened: GitHub's list of commits by path, GET /repos/{repo}/commits?sha=&path=, and each commit read fetched by its id, --depth 1) gives the commit that set the block its tip holds, and GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha} says whether it is the owner's website commit (committer web-flow, verified, author the owner); of those that are, the newer one's block must be the tranche's (the record check's ownerBlock)

conditions.what: Gate artifacts (gate-row) are kept at least 90 days.
conditions.why: merge trusts a gate row only when the run's artifact still holds it (verifyRow); an expired artifact makes a green gate unprovable.
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Actions, General: artifact and log retention); the gate workflow asks for 90 days
conditions.read: GET /repos/{repo}/actions/artifacts?name=gate-row: the newest artifact's expires_at less its created_at, in whole days; unmeasured when there is none yet

conditions.what: process/config.json on the tranche names the coordinator session of ROOT and the watcher.
conditions.why: ROOT's and the watcher's prompts name it as their coordinator session, besides Bob (PR 43). A job's coordinator is not this: job start names the addressed BOB (addresses/bob.json on the state branch), unless --coordinator overrides it.
conditions.who: BOB, through a pull request into the tranche
conditions.read: process/config.json on origin/<tranche>, through git: coordinator

conditions.what: The product's CLAUDE.md on the tranche carries the process lines of the pin's shims/CLAUDE.process.md exactly ({tranche} as the tranche's name: the pin, the one fetch command, where the role prompt comes from), below the owner's approvals block, and is under thirty lines without that block (TXT-1).
conditions.why: A session reads CLAUDE.md at its start; the approvals and these few lines are all it needs before its role prompt. The tool never writes the approvals block.
conditions.who: BOB, through a plain pull request into the tranche that adds the lines and leaves the approvals block as it is
conditions.read: CLAUDE.md on origin/<tranche>, through git, against the pin's shim, read from the process clone at the commit origin/<tranche> pins as .process (fetched by its id, --depth 1, when absent)

conditions.what: Each workflow under .github/workflows named like a shim of the pin equals that shim, and .claude/settings.json carries only the hooks the pin's shims/settings.hooks.json allows (SHM-1, ENF-1).
conditions.why: The gate and record shims are what make a merge trustworthy; a copy that drifted from the pin, or another hook, runs what the process did not review (ENF-1).

value.workflows: every shims/*.yml at the pin, as .github/workflows/<name>

conditions.who: BOB, through a plain pull request into the tranche that copies the pin's shim; a hook to remove is in the owner's settings file, which Bob changes through GitHub's website
conditions.read: the workflows and .claude/settings.json on origin/<tranche>, through git, against the pin's shims, read from the process clone at the tranche's .process pin

conditions.what: The checkout of the session running the check is the tranche's tip, with its approvals block: start check's own test.
conditions.why: A session acts on the owner's approvals only when CLAUDE.md is on the branch it starts from (10 of 10 with it, 2 of 10 without; Bob, 2 Nov, before the log; unverified). A runner started by hand from main held no approvals and was refused session starts. job start runs this check, so a session started from the wrong branch stops with a plain message.
conditions.value: HEAD is origin/<tranche>'s tip, and the approvals block in the checkout's file is the tip's
conditions.who: BOB and every session it starts: start from the tranche
conditions.read: start check (tool/lib/start.mjs) against the tranche: it fetches origin/<tranche> and compares HEAD and the approvals block with its tip; a checkout behind it says to pull the tranche or start from it

conditions.what: Every variable the product's process/config.json lists under "environment" (for example CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) is present in the environment of the session running the check.
conditions.why: The process deploys the product so walkers can run and each round can find and fix flaws, unattended; deploy tokens in the session environment are a standard condition (Bob, 2 Nov, before the log; unverified).
conditions.value: the names in process/config.json "environment"; not configured when the config lists none
conditions.who: the developer (the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: the environment of the session running the check: names only, never a value, a length or a prefix

conditions.what: When process/config.json names "cloudflare_account", the session's CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is that account.
conditions.why: Deploys must reach the product's own account and no other.
conditions.value: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID equals process/config.json cloudflare_account; not configured when the config names none
conditions.who: the developer (the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: the environment of the session running the check: a match, yes or no; only the configured account is printed; Cloudflare's API is not called

conditions.what: The session's CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN can read, in the account process/config.json names as cloudflare_account, Workers scripts, R2 buckets and containers: the scopes Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit and Containers Edit.
conditions.why: The product binds R2, Durable Objects, containers, service bindings, browser rendering and send_email, and no Workers KV, so the token asks for no KV scope (review follow-ups, 2 Nov). Without one, wrangler delete may exit with a Workers KV error after the delete itself succeeded; removing a development deployment counts that error as success only once a read of the script finds it gone (README, Development deployments).
conditions.who: the developer (a Cloudflare API token, saved in the Claude cloud environment's settings)
conditions.read: one harmless GET per scope (paths from Cloudflare's API reference, developers.cloudflare.com/api: Workers scripts, R2 buckets, Containers applications) on api.cloudflare.com/client/v4, the token given to curl on stdin: HTTP 200 with success true (or a bare JSON answer) is present; each scope reported present or missing; a read cannot tell Edit from Read; the token is never printed; not configured when the config names no cloudflare_account A 401 or 403, or a 200 with success false, is missing; a 429, a 5xx, another status or no answer is unknown (Cloudflare's status and retry-after printed), the condition unmeasured and no gap (C20). A present answer is kept per clone for an hour.

conditions.what: Every ruleset's bypass list is empty: no app, no deploy key, no role.
conditions.why: A session can read only whether its own account may bypass a ruleset; an app, deploy key or role in the list could carry a change around the rules.
conditions.value: bypass list empty on every ruleset
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Rules)
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: Workflows get a read-only token by default, and GitHub Actions may not create or approve pull requests.
conditions.why: Only the gate's post job and the branch cleanup's prune job (process-branch-prune.yml, contents: write, deleting nothing until Bob's approval sentence is in the approvals block) are given a write token, each by its own permissions block, and neither runs product code; nothing else in Actions can approve its own way into the tranche.
conditions.value: default workflow permissions: read; allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests: off
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Actions, General)
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: No Actions secret is given to the process workflows; the Cloudflare and release keys live in the jobs' cloud environment only.
conditions.why: The gate runs product code from any pull request; a secret it could read would leave with that code (decision 14, Bob, 2 Nov, before the log; unverified: jobs stay in the environment that holds the keys).
conditions.value: no repository or organization Actions secret used by process-gate or process-record
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Secrets and variables)
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: The developer is the only admin; the account sessions act as is a collaborator with Write.
conditions.why: Write lets sessions push their own branches and open pull requests; only the developer changes settings and rulesets.
conditions.value: the developer: admin; the session account: write; no one else
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Collaborators)
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: No deployment environment holds a secret that a pull request run, or a branch other than main, can reach.
conditions.why: An environment's secrets would otherwise reach product code run by the gate.
conditions.value: no environments, or each one limited to main
conditions.who: the developer (Settings, Environments)
conditions.read: confirmed once on the onboarding page

conditions.what: Each lanes row in process/config.json on the tranche that names a module has that module's ledger entry, its modules file row and its requirements file; a row without module stays valid.
conditions.why: A lane's module's marks are the lane's work (coordinator's ruling, 6 Nov); a lane naming a module with no entry starts nothing it can finish, and lane start refuses it.
conditions.value: each named module: process/ledger/<module>.json, a row in modules_file, its requirements file
conditions.who: BOB, through a plain pull request into the tranche (or dropping module from the lane's row)
conditions.read: process/config.json, the ledger entries, modules_file and the requirements files on origin/<tranche>, through git

conditions.what: process/config.json on the tranche names the product's internal walk (deploy.internal_walk.run), or records Bob's exemption ({"none": "<reason>", "by": "Bob, <date>"}).
conditions.why: The internal walk is required and tool-started at each round's close (Bob, 7 Nov: "Required, tool-started", run at "Round close only"); a product with none would close rounds unwalked.
conditions.value: deploy.internal_walk.run: an argv or a list of argvs; or the exemption, which reads "not configured: <reason>"
conditions.who: BOB, through a plain pull request into the tranche; an exemption only on Bob's word
conditions.read: process/config.json on origin/<tranche>, through git
